feedback: The confession follows the available distinction that led my vote: Justin invents neutralization even though the surviving correction only concerns ownership. It confirms taking poison at the preview and using the glass, which are new admissions of actions but not a newly introduced mechanism or evidentiary fact needed to understand the accusation. His desire to preserve the historical story and consequent destruction of his credibility makes the ending emotionally apt. Chip and Elle give concrete reasons for their documentary lies, helping competing suspicions resolve without magical exoneration. I find the ending earned as a plausible reconstruction, though the preview theft itself was never independently witnessed, so my earlier concern about circumstantial discrimination remains.
